long_biography.plain_text:
Bubalo grew up in Split in a family of economists whose company imported premium foods from neighbouring European markets. Business trips doubled as chances to visit marinas and study large passenger craft, while an economics degree supplied formal preparation. In his final university year, his father found a former fishing boat available after a Norwegian company failed and funded its purchase with Bubalo.

Bubalo created Mare Placidum to manage the conversion and took responsibility for offices, staff and the craft's transformation. He positioned the result as a boutique charter product rather than a low-cost group cruiser, then led structural and interior refits in 2019 and 2023. The project now combines coastal passenger transport, hospitality and a commercial charter model, with Bubalo continuing as company member, director and hands-on owner.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 100 through multiple independent exact-person bridges: the authoritative owner record links Luka Bubalo to 39.74-metre La Perla and an existing Mare Placidum LinkedIn profile; BOAT interviews him as the Croatian owner; FINA identifies him as current Mare Placidum member and director; and Croatian reporting and a ministry table connect Mare Placidum to the vessel.

The name is collision-prone. A Serbian venture-capital executive, Croatian banking professional, footballers and a Bosnian handball player were excluded because they lack the combined Mare Placidum, Split, La Perla and maritime-tourism anchors. No facts from those profiles are used.

Forbes-first research found no dedicated Forbes.com profile for the Croatian La Perla owner. Exact-name searches returned unrelated people and non-Forbes sources, so Forbes status is not_found and no Forbes social is proposed.

Hospitality is used for both wealth creation and current primary industry because Bubalo deliberately converted the vessel into a boutique charter and passenger-hospitality product and continues to direct the operating company. Shipping & Maritime describes the transport medium, but hospitality better captures the revenue proposition and customer-facing business model.

The reviewed sources do not publish Bubalo's personal net worth or a full asset inventory. Hospitality is assigned from the only clearly evidenced founder-owned operating platform, not from a wealth threshold or an assumption that the vessel represents all personal assets.

Self-made — advantaged start is directly supported. Bubalo created and managed Mare Placidum, but his parents' established food-import company supplied commercial experience and financial security, his father found the acquisition opportunity and his parents funded the purchase. No inherited completed charter business is evidenced.

Founder is used because Bubalo says he opened his own company for the conversion and remains its member and director. Ante Bubalo is also a current company member, so the dossier does not call Luka sole owner or sole controller.

Public sources variously describe La Perla as 39.7, 39.74 or 40 metres and as a former Norwegian or North Sea fishing vessel. These descriptions are consistent at normal editorial precision. The authoritative input's 399 gross tonnes was not independently confirmed by the reviewed public sources and remains an upstream specification only.

The BOAT profile says Bubalo's parents imported premium foods but does not name the family company or disclose its ownership, financial scale or Bubalo's formal role. The family business is therefore described only as a launch platform and funding source, not as his personal wealth-producing asset.

No reliable birth date or birthplace was found. BOAT says Bubalo grew up in Split, which does not establish birth there, so the blank place and date fields remain unproposed. The input's Croatia birth country is retained without expansion.

Male gender is proposed from the exact-person first-person profile's repeated male identification. No title, middle name, suffix, secondary nationality or secondary residence country met the evidence threshold.

The existing LinkedIn URL is verified by the exact Mare Placidum, Croatia, University of Split and Project La Perla anchors. It requires no correction and is therefore documented in sources rather than duplicated as a proposed social.

No verified official Instagram or person-controlled personal website was found. La Perla brokerage and brochure pages are commercial vessel materials rather than Bubalo's personal social profiles, so the missing priority fields remain unproposed.

Maritime tourism and Ship chartering are the minimum useful approved active tags. Passenger water transport and Luxury hospitality are true contextual descriptions but would add limited click-through value beyond the selected industry and business-model pair.

The 50-word short biography and 129-word long biography are source-invisible and sale-independent. The long biography has exactly two paragraphs, naturally discloses the material family advantage and excludes current prices, bookings, wealth estimates and vessel-sale discussion.
